title: Maximum Average Subarray I
summary: Given an integer array nums with n elements and an integer k, identify a contiguous subarray of length k with the highest average value.
statement: Given an integer array nums with n elements and an integer k, identify a contiguous subarray of length k with the highest average value. Return this average, with an allowable error of less than 10^-5.
constraints: Return the largest average among all contiguous subarrays of exactly k values.
reference_solution:
def maximum_fixed_average(nums, k):
    window = sum(nums[:k])
    best = window
    for index in range(k, len(nums)):
        window += nums[index] - nums[index - k]
        best = max(best, window)
    return best / k

def maximum_fixed_average(nums, k):
    window = sum(nums[:k])
    best = window
    for index in range(k, len(nums)):
        window += nums[index] - nums[index - k + 1]
        best = max(best, window)
    return best / k
hints: Adjacent fixed-length windows differ by one entering and one leaving value.
Maintain the current sum instead of recomputing every subarray.
Initialize the first k values; slide and track the largest sum; divide once.
All windows have the same denominator, so maximizing their sums also maximizes their averages.
